messages.author: 7193f20b09ee1b57
messages.subject: categorical variable
parts:
Dear lavaan users,

I tried to run a path analysis using lavaan, and a couple endogenous variables in my model were categorical. I saw lavaan release of .05 available and I wonder whether this release can handle categorical variables. 
Thank you!

Xu Zhang

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: categorical variable
parts:
On 09/19/2012 05:31 PM, xuzhang wrote:
>
> Dear lavaan users,
>
> I tried to run a path analysis using lavaan, and a couple endogenous
> variables in my model were categorical. I saw lavaan release of .05
> available and I wonder whether this release can handle categorical
> variables.

Yes it can. Using the three-stage weighted least squares approach (the
equivalent of estimator=WLSMV in Mplus). See the 'development' page on
the website for a few examples and the (ultra-short) section 8 of the
lavaanIntroduction.pdf document, available from the website.

Yves.

Dear Yves et al,
I am trying to compare IRT output with the ltm package to a CFA on lavaan. I am declaring my variables as ordered within the cfa function but I get the following error:
Error in if (rho == 0) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
I am not sure if there is something wrong with the data (something about the matrix of tetrachorics) or if there is a parameter that I am missing. The variables are dichotomous (0/1).
this is my cfa() syntax:

cfa.z <- cfa(mod, data=SAMPLE, estimator="WLSMV", ordered=names(SAMPLE)[2:11])
where:
> mod
[1] "f1 =~ INDFT+PRSPC+DPHNS+HONEY+ADDTN+FRQNC+DFNTL+INTRM+CLLLR+PHTGR"
> names(SAMPLE)[2:11]
 [1] "INDFT" "PRSPC" "DPHNS" "HONEY" "ADDTN" "FRQNC" "DFNTL" "INTRM" "CLLLR" "PHTGR"

Thanks for any feedback.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: categorical variable
parts:
On 09/25/2012 09:52 PM, Manolo Romero Escobar wrote:
> Dear Yves et al,
> I am trying to compare IRT output with the ltm package to a CFA on
> lavaan. I am declaring my variables as ordered within the cfa function
> but I get the following error:
>
> Error in if (rho == 0) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

This is a bug in 0.5-9, but has already been fixed in 0.5-10. It only
occurs if you have an empty cell in one of the pairwise tables. To
install the dev version, type in R:

install.packages("lavaan", repos="http://www.da.ugent.be", type="source")

If you still get this error (or if you have any other issues), let me know.

Yves.
